Tests duplicate adjacent values in the smallest non-trivial array, where values[0]=values[1] creates a degenerate butterfly input.
Tests overflow in the butterfly additions when a huge value (numeric_limits::max()/2) is introduced at a non-boundary index.
Tests a larger power-of-two with a monotonic decreasing sequence, exercising the bit-reversal with m=4 and multiple butterfly levels.
Tests the butterfly with all-equal negative values, where the FFT of [-1,-1] should be [-2,0], exercising sign handling with negative inputs.
Tests N=1 base case where both the DFT loop and bit-reversal guard are skipped; a candidate may hit shift-by-32 UB in bit reversal.
Tests sign handling in the butterfly with input [-1, 1] where the Nyquist bin should be -2, exposing twiddle-factor sign errors.
Tests constant input at the domain boundary; DC bin should be 4 and all other bins exactly 0, exposing accumulation or cancellation errors.
Tests full 3-stage butterfly and complete bit-reversal permutation with m=3, exercising all loop bounds and twiddle-factor squaring.
Tests large value (~8.99e307) propagation through butterfly additions, exposing precision loss or overflow in intermediate sums.

Introduces an extreme coordinate (~max/2) among normal-range values, potentially causing floating-point overflow in the cross product multiplication and testing Inf/NaN sign handling in the hull construction loops.
Targets the pointsSorted.size() == 2 early-return branch (returns 2*dist); a candidate guarding on original points.size() < 3 would incorrectly return 0, matching the documented BL-02 bug class.
Tests the minimum valid input size where the triple loop executes exactly once, including negative coordinates to verify sign handling in the area formula.
Tests all identical points at an even size, ensuring the implementation correctly returns 0 for degenerate triangles without division or early exit issues.
Tests alternating extreme values within the allowed domain to stress intermediate multiplication results and potential precision loss in the shoelace formula.
Tests duplicate adjacent points in the middle of a small array, which should yield a zero-area triangle and verify the loop bounds handle the last index correctly.
Minimal valid pair at opposite extremes of the domain, exercising the single-iteration loop and the distance formula with maximum coordinate differences (2000 each axis).
Small odd size with a duplicate at boundary k=0, testing off-by-one in duplicate placement and that distance-0 is correctly found among three pairs.
Targets sign handling in abs() with interleaved positive/negative values where the minimum distance is between same-sign elements at range extremes.
Targets odd size with non-symmetric distances, exposing candidates that omit abs() or return the first distance found instead of the minimum.
Targets the smallest valid input with maximum possible distance, exposing off-by-one loop bounds, incorrect minDist initialization, and missing abs() calls.
Empty matrix (N=0): tests zero-iteration base case and signed/unsigned loop comparison i < N when N is 0.
Single-element matrix: minimal non-empty case where off-by-one in either loop bound is most visible.
Smallest multi-element matrix: exposes row-major indexing errors A[i*N+j] vs A[j*N+i] with the smallest non-trivial stride.
Small odd size: catches candidates that assume even dimensions or use N/2 in indexing.
Matches the docstring example size (4x4): validates the canonical case the reference was designed around.
Small odd prime size: ensures loop bounds are inclusive of the last row/column without relying on power-of-two alignment.
Odd prime size: non-power-of-two stride stresses row-major address calculation A[i*N+j] for off-by-one in the inner loop.
Power-of-two size: candidates using bit-shifts or masking for indexing are exercised; also a common SIMD boundary.
Medium power-of-two: tests that int loop variable i does not overflow when multiplied by N (i*N up to ~1M) and that count accumulates correctly.
Maximum allowed size: stresses int i*N+j indexing (max ~16.7M, still within int range) and validates count does not overflow for dense matrices.
Empty graph (N=0) tests the loop bound and base case where no vertices are processed, ensuring the function returns 0 without crashing.
Single-vertex graph tests the recursion base case and 1x1 adjacency matrix indexing where the only entry is likely zero.
Small odd size tests odd loop bounds and DFS traversal on a graph small enough to have multiple components.
Small even size tests even loop bounds and row-major indexing for a small even N, catching off-by-one errors in neighbor iteration.
Small odd size (2^3-1) tests off-by-one in row-major indexing and component counting on a small graph.
Empty graph: outer loop never executes, tests base-case return of 0 and avoids any indexing into A.
Single-node graph: row sum is just A[0], exposes off-by-one in loop bound and self-loop handling.
Small even size matching the documented example, targets correct row-major indexing at minimal even dimension.
Small odd size to probe loop bounds and row-stride arithmetic on an odd NxN matrix.
Smallest non-trivial graph where DFS can recurse to a neighbor, testing the recursion base case and the A[node*N+i] indexing with N=2.
Small odd N tests the generator's spanning-path loop bound (i < N-1) and BFS neighbor iteration with an odd matrix dimension, exposing off-by-one errors.
Power-of-two size can expose candidate implementations that use bit-shift or power-of-2 assumptions in adjacency matrix row indexing (current*N + i).
Alternates between (0,0) and (1,1), testing the x>=0 && y>=0 boundary with exact zeros that random testing rarely produces, exposing candidates that use > instead of >=.
Power-of-two size targets SIMD/vectorized implementations that may mishandle loop remainders or boundary conditions at common vector widths.
One-less-than-alphabet-size boundary may expose off-by-one errors in bin initialization or loop-count logic in optimized implementations.
Tests exact quartile boundary values 0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 where strict `<` vs `<=` classification matters
Tests the else clause (bin[3]) with boundary value 0.75 across different integer parts to catch (int) cast and `<=` bugs
Small even size tests reduce with a minimal non-trivial even partition, exposing off-by-one or chunk-boundary bugs in candidate loop or parallel implementations.
Small odd size exercises the parity-sensitive XOR reduction path where an odd count of true values yields true, a case plain random tests at larger sizes may under-sample.
Minimal even size with non-trivial values; if even/odd inversion logic is flipped, result is 2 instead of 0.5.
Even size with all identical values; tests that x * 1/x pairs cancel to 1 across multiple inversions.
Even size with alternating boundary values; tests multiple inversions of max value and accumulation of tiny products.
Odd size with alternating extremes; tests that odd-indexed 1s act as identity and even-indexed 100s accumulate to a large product.
Fractional values expose int accumulator bug where std::reduce with int init 0 truncates each element to 0, yielding avg 0 instead of 0.5.
Sum 100 not divisible by size 3, exposing integer division (33 vs 33.33) and off-by-one divisor errors.
Both boundary values of the domain in one input, testing extreme value handling in the reduce summation.
All-zero input with odd size tests zero-sum division and ensures no spurious NaN from 0/3.
Duplicate maximum values test equal-element handling and potential overflow in accumulation.
Ascending ramp producing a non-integer average exposes integer division and tests ordered input summation.
All even numbers with no odd present; reference returns INT_MAX sentinel, exposing candidates that return 0 or -1 for no-odd-found.
All elements equal to 7 (odd); exercises the else branch (a >= b) of the reduce lambda with duplicate odd values.
All even except the last element which is 1 (smallest odd); tests full-array scan and correct identification of the minimum odd at the boundary.
Tests the minimal non-empty case where an off-by-one loop bound or incorrect SIMD remainder handling would yield 0 instead of the single-element min.
Introduces numeric_limits::max()/2 alongside small random values, exposing overflow or precision loss in accumulation that plain random tests within [0,100] cannot reach.
Alternating extreme signs produce exact zero crossings in the prefix sum, exposing sign-handling and inclusive-vs-exclusive scan bugs.
Odd size with a negative-to-positive ramp drives the cumulative sum negative then back toward zero, testing sign transitions and off-by-one loop bounds.
Leading and trailing zeros with a non-zero middle element verify zero elements are accumulated rather than skipped or zeroed.
Descending order means each element is the new running minimum, so output must equal input—exposes off-by-one bugs that fail to include the current index.
Tests duplicate/equal elements and sign-change propagation where the running minimum must persist through later larger values.
Tests minimal non-empty all-zero input; catches initialization bugs and zero-handling edge cases where prefix sums and total sum should all be zero.
Tests sign handling with alternating extreme values where prefix sums cancel to zero mid-array, catching exclusive-vs-inclusive scan and sign accumulation errors.
Tests inclusive scan with identical large positive values; catches off-by-one errors where exclusive scan would yield a different sum.
Tests degenerate value_range (only valid for all_same) with all-negative constant, exposing sign-handling and constant-accumulation bugs.
Tests a large value (INT_MAX/2) at the first position with minimal size, exposing overflow and large-value handling bugs.
Single negative element: exposes base-case loop bound and INT_MIN-vs-zero initialization bugs.
All zeros yields answer 0, exposing implementations that incorrectly return INT_MIN or skip zero-sum subarrays.
Degenerate all-negative constant array: answer is the constant itself, exposing init-to-zero and reset-on-negative Kadane bugs.
Whole-array sum is optimal despite interleaved negatives, exposing prefix-exclusion and early-reset bugs.
All pages >= 100 so no short book is found, testing the return books.size() sentinel path that a candidate might confuse with 0 or -1.
Only index 0 has pages < 100 while index 1 has exactly 100, testing both strict less-than boundary and backward loop reaching index 0.
Two-element vector with both boundary values of the allowed range, exercising the shortest non-trivial loop and extreme value handling.
Degenerate range forces every element to the identical value 7, exercising all-duplicate handling that random fills almost never produce.
Single element: loop body never executes, tests base case initialization.
Two equal elements closest to PI: strict < means index 0 wins, catches <= vs < bugs.
Minimum (closest to PI) at last index: loop must update min and index.
Minimum at middle index: tests that loop correctly finds non-endpoint minimum.
Tie at first and last index: strict < returns 0, catches <= returning last index.
Degenerate range with all_same: all elements equal to 100, no loop update ever occurs.
Minimum at index 3 with odd size: tests finding min at a non-special position with multiple preceding non-minimal values.
Two identical values at indices 0 and 1 are equidistant from PI; tests strict-less-than tie-breaking where reference returns index 0 but a candidate using <= would return index 1.
Even at index 3 after multiple odds: catches operator-precedence bug in x[i] & 1 == 0 which would falsely return 0.
All odd values: tests the not-found path returning x.size(), which random tests rarely hit for larger sizes.
Only the last element is even: catches off-by-one in loop bound such as i < size-1 that would skip the final index.
All even values: verifies return of index 0 rather than last even index or count of evens.
Tests single-element containers; catches off-by-one loop bounds like i < size()-1 that skip the only element.
Tests small container with numeric_limits::max()/2 spike at position 0; catches integer overflow in value comparisons and sign-handling bugs.
Tests linear search on a minimal two-element ascending ramp spanning negative to positive values, complementing the existing descending spec and exercising sign-boundary handling in comparisons.
Empty vector exercises std::sort on a zero-length range, exposing off-by-one or null-dereference bugs in loop bounds that random non-empty tests would never reach.
Single-element input tests the minimal base case where k must equal 1.
Two elements at opposite range extremes test boundary value handling and smallest non-trivial partition.
All identical values test whether partition-based selection handles equal elements without infinite loops.
Two zeros test duplicate minimum values in the smallest non-trivial case.
Pre-sorted odd-size array tests quickselect worst-case pivot selection behavior.
Reverse-sorted even-size array tests partition robustness with monotonically decreasing input.
Max-value duplicates surrounding the minimum test duplicate handling at range extremes.
Forced adjacent duplicate pair in a random array tests whether partition correctly processes equal neighbors.

Tests positive/negative zero equality under the sort comparator; -0.0 and 0.0 are equal under operator< but have different bit patterns, exposing candidates that use bit-level or memcmp-based comparison.
Empty vector base case: sort on zero elements exercises loop-bound and iterator edge cases.
Single-element input: no comparisons performed, tests early-return / trivial-size handling.
Minimal reverse-sorted pair: forces exactly one swap, the smallest non-trivial sort operation.
Two equal start times: comparator must return false both ways, tests strict-weak-ordering correctness.
Small odd size with one adjacent swap: exercises partitioning and insertion-style fixup in introsort.
Large startTime near INT_MAX/2 in the middle: exposes overflow in subtraction-based comparators (a.startTime - b.startTime).
Odd size with extreme lo/hi alternation: maximizes misprediction and tests median-of-three pivot selection.
Mid-size with adjacent equal keys near center: stresses equal-element partitioning and potential infinite-loop bugs.
Minimal pair: tests off-by-one in both collection and write-back loops with exactly two elements.
Smallest odd size: exercises boundary where a zero in the middle splits non-zero elements around it.
Small even size: tests stable placement when zeros and non-zeros interleave across an even-length vector.
Small odd size with more slots: increases probability of duplicate non-zero values and multiple zeros interacting.
Power-of-two size: common internal sort partition boundary that can expose implementation-specific sort bugs.
Maximum allowed size: stress-tests index overflow tendencies (int i vs size_t) and large-scale zero/duplicate handling.
Tests empty system base case: no loop iterations execute, x.assign(0) creates empty vector, and candidate may crash on unsigned underflow when computing N-1 for back-substitution loop index.
Tests minimal non-empty system with single division in back-substitution; sparse generator may produce zero diagonal element, exposing division-by-zero and NaN/inf propagation differences.
Smallest system where pivot search, row swapping, and forward elimination all execute, testing the core Gaussian elimination path including swap logic.
Small system with multiple elimination steps and multi-iteration back-substitution, testing iterative correctness and dependency chain in the full algorithm.
Large system stressing dense NxN matrix allocation (~128MB) and O(N^3) elimination, exposing memory allocation failures, performance bugs, and signed/unsigned index transitions.
Alternating extreme signs (-1, 1, -1) stress sign handling and potential cancellation when multiple column-row matches cause contributions to the same output cell.
All elements share the same negative value, testing uniform sign handling and exposing candidates that drop or flip signs when values are identical.
Tests the minimal non-empty case (size 1) with a non-zero constant value, targeting off-by-one errors in the beta-scaling and COO iteration loops.
Tests sign handling with alternating -1 and 1 values, targeting accumulation bugs when positive and negative contributions cancel.
Tests single-element vectors with a negative degenerate value_range, exercising minimal loop iteration, sign handling, and the all_same degenerate-range code path.
Tests empty matrix base case where no loop iterations execute and L/U must be zero-length
Tests minimal 1x1 case where k-loops never execute and only diagonal L[0]=1 and U[0]=A[0][0] are set
Tests smallest case with one k-loop iteration, exercising the subtraction and division branches
Tests multiple k-loop iterations (up to 2), checking accumulation correctness in U and L updates
Small even size testing balanced loop iterations and off-by-one in j>=i vs i>j branch conditions
Small odd size testing asymmetric loop behavior and diagonal assignment L[i*N+i]=1 after inner loop
Prime size that may expose size-dependent bugs in index arithmetic i*N+j or loop bounds
Power-of-2 size testing potential alignment or power-of-2 specific optimization bugs
One less than power of 2, boundary case for size-dependent implementations and loop termination
Power of 2, larger size testing floating-point accumulation across many k-loop iterations
Tests the ==1 literal check (value 2 must not count as a neighbor) and diagonal neighbor counting (8-neighbor vs 4-neighbor) at the center cell whose only 1-neighbor is diagonal.
Tests boundary zero-padding with an extreme value (numeric_limits::max()/2) at the left boundary in a minimal 2-element array, exposing off-by-one neighbor access and potential overflow in summation.
Tests sign handling with extreme opposite values where boundary outputs are exactly zero due to cancellation, exposing sign-handling bugs in boundary computation.
Tests the 2x2 grid where every element is a corner, exercising all four boundary zero-padding branches simultaneously with alternating signs.

Corner-only alive cells in 4x4 grid: non-wrapping gives all-zero output (each corner has 0 live neighbors), but wrapping implementations would keep corners alive (3 live neighbors each), exposing boundary-mode bugs.
Tests the exact-zero boundary of ReLU at a typical SIMD width, which random tests almost never hit.
Tests subnormal-magnitude values straddling zero and domain endpoints, exposing sign-handling bugs at the ReLU threshold.
Single odd element at minimum value: tests loop base case and odd negation branch with smallest input.
Single even element at maximum value: tests even halving branch with largest input and boundary value.
Minimal two-element pair exercising both branches (odd then even) to catch off-by-one in loop bounds.
Small odd-sized array with odd-even-odd pattern using both boundary values to test branch switching.
All identical even values with degenerate range: tests uniform even-branch processing and duplicate handling.
Strict odd/even alternation at boundary values with odd size: stress-tests rapid branch switching and loop count.
Example-like input with 100 substituted for 0: validates spec example behavior within allowed value domain.
Tests uniform division by zero; reference yields -inf for every element, exposing candidates that crash, guard with epsilon, or produce NaN.
Tests signed-zero division (±0.0 yield ∓inf), sign handling (x=-1 → 2), and domain boundary values (±50) in a single surgical case.
Tests signed integer overflow: spike value numeric_limits<int>::max()/2 squared overflows int, exposing candidates that use wider intermediate types.
Tests sign handling at domain boundaries: negative values must square to positive, and both extremes of the allowed range are exercised.
Tests consistent sign handling across an even-sized array with alternating extreme negative and positive values that all square to the same result.
Single-element array tests loop off-by-one (i=0 only) and the smallest power of two where x-1 wraps to 0.
Upper boundary of the allowed domain: 1024 is the largest power of two in range and 1025 is one past it, testing the transition at the domain edge.
Exhaustive list of every power of two in [1,1025]; a candidate with an off-by-one in the bit trick will fail on at least one of these.
Degenerate range producing a constant non-power-of-two array; tests that the candidate returns uniformly false and handles lo==hi correctly.
Surgical mix: 1 and 2 catch x&1 or x&(x+1) bugs on true cases, 3 and 6 catch the same bugs on false cases, 1024 tests a large power of two.
